whatWeChecked: The broker relationship: which partner desk executes orders.
The asset list: how many pairs are actually offered.
The registration flow: what personal details the form collects.
The risk disclosure: where the capital-at-risk wording sits.
The security claims: encryption and account protection statements.
The withdrawal path: steps and any fees the page omits.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Register with your name, email and phone number, and confirm via the email you are sent.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Send the US$300 starting deposit through one of the accepted methods.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set your preferences, select automatic or manual execution, and run the practice account first.

pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
Risk settings before the first trade.
A browser dashboard - nothing to install.
cons: Marketing numbers that the fine print walks back.
No independent audit of the models.
redFlags: Support figures that contradict each other.
Template placeholders left unrendered.
Return claims without verification.

faqs.a: The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$300 minimum.
12 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.
Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$300 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.

bottomLine: The platform itself is workable - the dashboard, the demo and the two trading modes are all present. The caution applies to the claims around them, not the mechanics.
Our 4.7 reflects what the pages publish and what they skip. It is not a warning off - it is a reminder to trade the product, not the pitch.
